q: Which three facts do you need before writing a two-year scheme of work?
o: Guided learning hours, exam series and real teaching weeks
Student names, school colours and room numbers
Textbook prices, bus routes and holiday dates only
Grade boundaries, last year's marks and parents' jobs
why: These facts show how much time you really have and when the exam is.

q: Why should you record mock exam marks by exercise as well as the total?
o: It shows which exercises and skills need reteaching
why: Exercise-level records show where marks are lost.

q: Roughly, how many guided learning hours does the syllabus plan for?
why: The syllabus is designed around about 130 guided learning hours as guidance.

q: Which Cambridge learner attribute is described as 'using a range of language to communicate ideas and information effectively in writing and speaking'?
why: This is the description of the confident learner.

q: Which route is most suitable first for a teacher who is new to Cambridge?
why: Introductory training helps new teachers understand the syllabus and assessment.

q: Where do Cambridge teachers find the Principal Examiner Report for Teachers and Results Analysis?
o: Cambridge support resources such as the School Support Hub
Only at the end of year concert
why: The Results area of Cambridge support offers these resources.

q: What is the best description of the 2024 to 2026 Listening paper?
why: Paper 2 is 100 per cent multiple choice with 40 marks.

q: What happened to tiers in the 2024 to 2026 syllabus?
o: Tiers were only used for Speaking
why: The changes section says tiering has been removed from the qualification.

q: Which phrase from the syllabus is a way of giving an example when speaking?
why: The syllabus lists 'just to name a few' for exemplifying.

q: Which pair are linking words that show contrast?
why: However and whereas show contrast. Therefore and consequently show result.

q: A student reads slowly because they try to understand every word. Which strategy helps most?
o: Teach skimming, scanning and guessing meaning from context
Ask them to read the text three times
Tell them to avoid long texts
Give them a dictionary in the exam
why: Dictionaries are not allowed and strategies save time in 400 to 650 word texts.

q: In Paper 2 Exercise 4 there are six speakers and eight statements. What does this mean for students?
o: Two statements are not used, so students can cross out used ones
Every statement must be used once
why: Six speakers match six statements, so two statements are not used.

q: Which is the best use of the one-minute preparation in Speaking Part 2?
o: Choose three ideas and an example in your head, without notes
Read the card aloud to the examiner
why: Candidates are not allowed to write notes during preparation.

q: In writing marking, what do you do after choosing the best-fit level?
o: Choose the mark inside the level: top, middle or lowest
why: Convincingly meets: highest mark. Adequately: middle. Just meets: lowest.

q: Which is a common teacher marking error?
o: Giving marks for effort or length instead of the mark scheme
why: Marks must follow the mark scheme only.

q: A student's short answer has a small spelling error but the meaning is clear. What is the usual rule?
o: Give the mark, since spelling is not tested there
why: Spelling and grammar are judged only where the question tests them, if meaning is unambiguous.

q: In Exercise 3, 'renting an e-bike' written as a policy in Question 8 earns:
o: 0 marks, it is the writer's own action
why: It belongs under what the writer has tried, Question 9.

q: Which statement matches Level 5 Development in the Speaking marking criteria?
o: Responses are relevant and consistently well developed; communication is maintained with ease
Responses are mostly relevant but limited
why: That is the Level 5 (9 to 10 marks) wording.

q: What should you do if more than one teacher in your centre marks Speaking?
o: Carry out internal moderation so all candidates are marked to the same standard
Mark separately and send different marks
Ask students to mark each other
why: Cambridge requires moderation or standardisation when more than one teacher marks.

q: Which of these must be true of the Speaking test recording?
o: It must be recorded in full for every candidate
Only the best candidates need a recording
why: The test must be recorded in full for all candidates.

q: Which is NOT a Speaking marking criterion?
why: The four criteria are grammar, vocabulary, development and pronunciation.

q: Which feedback is most helpful to a student?
o: Two or three specific targets linked to a skill and an action
A long list of every error
why: Specific, limited targets with actions help students improve.

q: What is the aim of a standardisation meeting?
why: Standardisation creates consistent marking.

q: A student writes a very long email far above the word range. What is likely?
o: Accuracy and control may suffer, and length alone earns no extra marks
why: Marks are for relevance, development and control of language, not length.

q: What is a distractor in multiple choice?
o: A wrong option that looks attractive
why: Distractors may use words from the text but give the wrong meaning.
